# `landiskaux` — PASS 1: landisk's wdc alt-status register is mapped 0x1da bytes from where the guest writes, and the fix is one `case`

## READ THIS FIRST — PLEASE DO NOT SIMPLY RATIFY

A recent panel had seven of nine seats confirm a premise this brief's author stated wrongly.
**Check the premises, not just the derivations.** Where I state something as fact, ask whether it
is true. A seat that re-derives a premise from something this brief did NOT give it is worth more
than a seat that agrees.

**THE TREE UNDER REVIEW IS `GXEMUL-SEC/src/`.** There are THREE pristine-2021-upstream copies of
GXemul under the project root (`./src/` and two under `_archive/audit-results-*/builds/`). They
are NOT this fork. If your line numbers disagree with mine by hundreds you are reading one of

**If you cannot read files that is expected** — every fact you need is inlined. Name any premise
you cannot settle from this packet rather than guessing at it.

**Where this brief states an ARITHMETIC claim — an address, a span, an offset — ENUMERATE it
rather than reasoning about it.** A derivation that skips one multiplier reads exactly like a

## 1. PREMISES ALREADY SETTLED, RE-INLINED SO NOBODY SPENDS AN ANSWER RE-DERIVING THEM

Settled 2026-09-18 by opening each file (re-derive any of them; do not take them from me):

* **`dev_wdc.c:2098` switches on `devinit->machine->machine_type` with exactly THREE cases** —
  `MACHINE_MACPPC` (`+0x160`), `MACHINE_HPCMIPS` (a hardcoded `0x14000386`, itself guarded on
  `devinit->addr == 0x14000180` and carrying a `/* TODO: Fix */`), and `MACHINE_IQ80321`
  (`+0x402`). **There is no `MACHINE_LANDISK`.**
* **There is NO `default:` arm.** The switch ends at `:2110` with a bare `}`. The value comes from
  a PRE-SWITCH initialisation at `:2095`: `alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x206;`. *(The queue
  row said "falls through to the default"; the substance is right and the word is not, and it
  matters here because a `case` that assigns nothing simply keeps `:2095`'s value.)*
* **`alt_status_addr` is NOT inside the main device mapping.** `:2120` registers a SEPARATE
  **two-byte** device, `"wdc_altstatus"`, at that address. `:2122` registers the main device at
  `devinit->addr` for `DEV_WDC_LENGTH * devinit->addr_mult` bytes.
* **`DEV_WDC_LENGTH` is 8** (`dev_wdc.c:45`), and **landisk passes `addr_mult=2`** — read from the
  device string itself at `machine_landisk.c:87-88`:
  `"wdc irq=%s.cpu[%i].irq[0x%x] addr_mult=2 addr=0x14000000"`.
* **`devinit->addr_mult` exists** (`src/include/device.h:53`, `int addr_mult`) and `dev_wdc.c`
  already uses it at `:1174` (`relative_addr /= d->addr_mult`), `:2083` and `:2123`.
* **`MACHINE_LANDISK` is 6004** (`src/include/machine.h:268`).

Settled 2026-08-27 by a MEASURED BOOT CENSUS (`regress/artifacts/landiskaux/census_20260827/`),
which this brief's first draft did not carry — the omission it exists to avoid:

* **OpenBSD 7.6 issues exactly TWELVE byte writes to `0x1400002c` and ZERO reads**, reproduced on
  FOUR runs across TWO independent instruments (three pristine boots, one census-hook build).
* All twelve are `len=1`, all from `pc=0x8c15f6e8 <obio_iomem_write_1+0x8>`, all `no_exceptions=0`
  — **real guest stores, not debugger reads.**
* Six carry `0x08` (WDCTL_4BIT), five `0x02` (WDCTL_IDS), and **the FIRST carries `0x0c` =
  `WDCTL_RST | WDCTL_4BIT` — a real ATA SOFT RESET, silently discarded today.**
* **LIVENESS CONTROL from the same boot:** the command block at `0x14000000..0x1400000f` SUCCEEDS
  — 12,718 accesses, `wd0` attaches with correct geometry — so `devinit->addr` is RIGHT and the
  defect is a missing offset case, not a wrong base.
* `wdc_altstatus` at `0x14000206` receives **ZERO accesses for the entire boot.**

Settled 2026-09-11 by a codex FIX-DESIGN run (`codex_fixdesign_20260911.txt`), each re-checked here:

* `dev_wdc_altstatus_access` does **NOT** divide `relative_addr` by `addr_mult` — it tests
  `relative_addr != 0` and nothing else. **So the primary's two-byte stride does not require a
  two-byte auxiliary registration.**
* **Twelve one-byte writes at offset 0 cannot distinguish a length-1 from a length-2
  registration** — already filed as `wdcaltwidth`.
* **Direct calls to the auxiliary handler cannot test the missing machine case**, since they
  bypass init and address dispatch.
* Codex **declined to derive the replacement address from the permitted files**, calling it
  "Verified `A`". *That refusal is the live question this panel inherits — see Q2.*

**THE ARITHMETIC, enumerated rather than asserted:**

    main wdc device : 0x14000000 .. 0x14000000 + 8*2 - 1  =  0x14000000..0x1400000f   (16 bytes)
                      -- which is exactly what machine_landisk.c:86's own comment claims,
                         "wdc0 at obio0 port 0x14000000-0x1400000f irq 10"
    altstatus TODAY : 0x14000000 + 0x206                  =  0x14000206   (2 bytes)
    guest WRITES    : 0x1400002c                          (twelve measured Device Control writes)
    fix would give  : 0x14000000 + 0x16 * 2               =  0x1400002c
    collision check : 0x2c = 44 >= 16, so the two-byte altstatus lands BEYOND the main span.
                      NO COLLISION.  (Nobody had run this check; it is the one that could have
                      made the fix register a device inside an existing one.)

## 2. THE FULL ENCLOSING BLOCK (comments trimmed; every exit path shown)

```c
	alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x206;

	/*  Special hacks for individual machines:  */
	switch (devinit->machine->machine_type) {
	case MACHINE_MACPPC:
		alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x160;
		break;
	case MACHINE_HPCMIPS:
		/*  TODO: Fix  */
		if (devinit->addr == 0x14000180)
			alt_status_addr = 0x14000386;
		break;
	case MACHINE_IQ80321:
		alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x402;
		break;
	}

	/*  Get disk geometries:  */
	for (i=0; i<2; i++)
		if (diskimage_exist(devinit->machine, d->base_drive +i, DISKIMAGE_IDE))
			diskimage_getchs(devinit->machine, d->base_drive + i,
			    DISKIMAGE_IDE, &d->cyls[i], &d->heads[i], &d->sectors_per_track[i]);

	memory_device_register(devinit->machine->memory, "wdc_altstatus",
	    alt_status_addr, 2, dev_wdc_altstatus_access, d, DM_DEFAULT, NULL);
	memory_device_register(devinit->machine->memory, devinit->name,
	    devinit->addr, DEV_WDC_LENGTH * devinit->addr_mult, dev_wdc_access,
	    d, DM_DEFAULT, NULL);
```

## 3. THE PROPOSED FIX — one `case`, and it is the whole diff

```c
	case MACHINE_LANDISK:
		alt_status_addr = devinit->addr + 0x16 * devinit->addr_mult;
		break;
```

---

## 4. THE QUESTIONS

**Q1 — IS THE MULTIPLIER FORM RIGHT, OR SHOULD IT BE A LITERAL?** The three existing cases all use
a BARE offset (`+0x160`, `+0x402`) or a hardcoded absolute (`0x14000386`); **not one of them
multiplies by `addr_mult`.** So the prescribed line is the only case of its kind in the switch. Is
`0x16 * addr_mult` the right shape — it tracks the register-spacing the machine declares — or is
the house idiom here a plain `+ 0x2c`, with the multiplier an over-generalisation from a single
data point? *Both resolve to the same address today; they differ only if a future landisk variant
declares a different `addr_mult`.*

**Q2 — WHERE DOES 0x16 COME FROM, AND IS IT LOAD-BEARING?** The claim is that the OpenBSD 7.6
driver writes `0x1400002c`, and `0x2c / 2 == 0x16`. **A wrong multiplier maps the register
SILENTLY** — no crash, no diagnostic, just a control register nobody reads. What independent
evidence fixes 0x16 rather than 0x2c-as-a-literal? Is there an SH4/landisk source that states the
alt-status/Device-Control register's offset in *register units*?

**Q3 — THE WITNESS.** *The row recorded `witness: none` until today, and a measured rung-4 boot
census had been sitting in its own artifacts directory since 2026-08-27 — corrected before this
brief was fired.*  What remains genuinely open is clause (i): a rung-2..4 witness is INVALID
unless it shows the symptom pre-fix AND goes green post-fix **with the same script**.  Only the
pre-fix half can exist yet. **That is an argument about ONE instrument, not a demonstration that no guest-path
witness exists.** Per this project's 2026-08-27 lifecycle ruling, a round may not be recorded as
rung-1 until one seat has been asked to try a rung-3 probe — and the last time that ask was made, a
seat built a witness in a SINGLE invocation. **Can a rung-3 probe reach this?** A guest store to
`0x1400002c` on unmodified `-E landisk` should be swallowed today and answered by `wdc_altstatus`
after the fix; a store to `0x14000206` should show the mirror image. If you can name that probe,
say so concretely; if you are confident none exists, say why in terms that are not about the
offline differential.

**Q4 — THE OPTION SET.** This is an ADDITION to product code, and the ADDITION LICENCE says
additions are licensed by a MEASURED DELTA or a TRANSFERRED WARRANT, never by "it cannot hurt".
The claimed delta is twelve measured Device Control writes landing on unmapped memory. **Is that
delta real and is the addition the right member?** Name the members you would consider — including
ones this brief has not: is there a case for fixing `machine_landisk.c` instead (declare the
altstatus address at the machine, not in the device), or for the HPCMIPS-style absolute?

**Q5 — WHAT IS THE SMALLEST EDIT** to the block in §2 that breaks a property this fix claims and
still passes whatever detector ships with it? And — separately — **does adding a fourth `case`
create any hazard for the existing three?** Note `MACHINE_HPCMIPS` already guards on
`devinit->addr == 0x14000180` while landisk's addr is `0x14000000`: close, and worth checking that
no machine reaches two arms.

[machine_landisk.c:86](C:/DocumentNoSnc/CC/GXEMUL/GXEMUL-SEC/src/machines/machine_landisk.c:86), [dev_wdc.c:1082](C:/DocumentNoSnc/CC/GXEMUL/GXEMUL-SEC/src/devices/dev_wdc.c:1082), [dev_wdc.c:2030](C:/DocumentNoSnc/CC/GXEMUL/GXEMUL-SEC/src/devices/dev_wdc.c:2030)

Neither the SH-4 identification nor the two-byte stride specifies how the board selects that separate bank. `machine_landisk.c` supplies no auxiliary-bank base or board address-decode definition. **3.** I checked the entire initializer, **lines 1981�?"2040**. Once the correct address is established, a LANDISK-specific assignment followed by `break` is sufficient for **address selection in this function**.

The control flow after the switch is straightforward:

- Fetch disk geometries using `d->base_drive`.
- Register the auxiliary device using `alt_status_addr`.
- Register the primary device using `devinit->addr` and `devinit->addr_mult`.
- Install the tick function, set `devinit->return_ptr`, and return success.

`alt_status_addr` has no later overwrite and only one subsequent use: the auxiliary registration. No later calculation requires it to retain `B + 0x206`. **4.** Assuming the filed accesses successfully translate to an **unregistered physical address outside RAM**, they follow the unimplemented-address path, not the registered-device failure path.

Device dispatch requires `baseaddr <= paddr < endaddr`. If no device matches, execution leaves the search without calling any device callback. [memory_rw.c:480](C:/DocumentNoSnc/CC/GXEMUL/GXEMUL-SEC/src/cpus/memory_rw.c:480), [memory_rw.c:629](C:/DocumentNoSnc/CC/GXEMUL/GXEMUL-SEC/src/cpus/memory_rw.c:629)

For an address at or above `mem->physical_max`:

- Without `NO_EXCEPTIONS`, it calls `memory_warn_about_unimplemented_addr(...)`.
- If that helper returns nonzero, memory access returns `MEMORY_ACCESS_FAILED`.
- Otherwise the write reaches `do_return_ok` without a store and returns `MEMORY_ACCESS_OK`.
- With `NO_EXCEPTIONS`, the helper is skipped and that write also takes the success exit.

The zero-filling in this block applies only to **reads**. [memory_rw.c:662](C:/DocumentNoSnc/CC/GXEMUL/GXEMUL-SEC/src/cpus/memory_rw.c:662), [memory_rw.c:784](C:/DocumentNoSnc/CC/GXEMUL/GXEMUL-SEC/src/cpus/memory_rw.c:784)

**The helper�?Ts definition is absent from the permitted files.** Therefore its diagnostic visibility, architecture-specific effects, and return value for LANDISK cannot be established here. An unconditional claim of �?otwelve silent successes,�?? �?otwelve warnings,�?? or �?otwelve guest faults�?? would exceed the evidence. A host warning also does not itself constitute a guest exception.

By comparison, a **registered** callback returning zero has its result converted to `-1`, enters the failure branch when exceptions are enabled, and returns failure. It never resumes the device search or falls through to unassigned-address handling. Furthermore, the explicit exception calls there are guarded by `MEM_MIPS` and `MEM_M88K`; the MIPS `EXCEPTION_DBE` conclusion must not be transferred to SH-4. [memory_rw.c:583](C:/DocumentNoSnc/CC/GXEMUL/GXEMUL-SEC/src/cpus/memory_rw.c:583)

| Required evidence | What it distinguishes |
|---|---|
| Twelve actual guest-issued stores in the defined witness interval, recording writer PC, virtual/physical address, direction, original length, and byte value | A run in which the guest never issued the stores |

"""wdcaltoffset -- RUNG-3 WITNESS AND DETECTOR.  Real guest instructions, real address
decode, real memory_rw, on an UNMODIFIED in-tree machine description (evbmips -e malta).

THE DEFECT.  DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc_altstatus) in src/devices/dev_wdc.c reads relative_addr
ZERO times, while dev_wdc_init registers its region TWO BYTES WIDE.  The durable keys are
grep anchors, not line numbers:

    grep -n 'DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc_altstatus)'   src/devices/dev_wdc.c
    grep -n '"wdc_altstatus",'               src/devices/dev_wdc.c

        memory_device_register(..., "wdc_altstatus", alt_status_addr, 2,
            dev_wdc_altstatus_access, d, DM_DEFAULT, NULL);

    offset 0  ->  0x3f6  Device Control      (write: nIEN, SRST, 4BIT)
    offset 1  ->  0x3f7  Drive Address Reg   READ-ONLY on real ATA hardware

Both offsets land in the same handler body, so a guest STORE to 0x3f7 is executed as a
store to Device Control.  Since #481 corrected the arm's bit to WDCTL_RST and wired in
wdc_new_command_reset(), that store now performs a full soft reset: write_in_progress is
cleared and the input ring is purged.  A write to a register the guest is not even
allowed to write aborts a live ATA WRITE SECTORS and destroys its staged bytes.

THE MACHINE IS NOT MODIFIED AND NO DEVICE IS ADDED.  malta carries a wdc through its own
committed path: machine_evbmips.c bus_pci_add(..., "piix4_ide") -> bus_pci.c
PCIINIT(piix4_ide), which does device_add(machine, "wdc addr=<isa_portbase+0x1f0> ...")
whenever an IDE image is attached; isa_portbase = 0x18000000.  Attaching a disk image is
ordinary operation, not a machine edit.

    wdc registers      physical 0x180001f0 + N  ->  KSEG1 0xffffffffb80001f0 + N
    wdc_altstatus      physical 0x180003f6      ->  KSEG1 0xffffffffb80003f6
    the read-only reg  physical 0x180003f7      ->  KSEG1 0xffffffffb80003f7

THE SHAPE OF THE WITNESS -- three phases, IDENTICAL except for the address of one store.

    PHASE 1  poke 0x06 (nIEN|SRST) at 0x3f6, the REAL Device Control register.
             A legitimate soft reset.  BOTH builds must abort the armed write.
             This is the ACCEPT control the de-escalation clause demands: it proves the
             fix leg does not disable the register it is supposed to leave alone, and it
             proves the reset machinery this probe observes is alive.

    PHASE 2  poke the SAME 0x06 at 0x3f7, the READ-ONLY Drive Address Register.
             *** THE DEFECT.  Committed build: identical to phase 1.  Fix leg: nothing
             happens. ***

    PHASE 3  poke 0x02 (nIEN alone, WDCTL_RST clear) at 0x3f7.
             Neither build resets.  This is the discriminator that says the defect is
             the RESET BIT reaching a register that has none, rather than "any store to
             0x3f7 does something".

PHASE 1 AND PHASE 2 ARE THE ANCHOR (vacuity-floor clause (f)).  They are the same
stimulus at ADJACENT addresses, so the pair pins WHERE the store lands, not merely that
two addresses behave differently.  On the committed build the two phases are
indistinguishable -- which IS the defect, stated as a measurement.

THE TWO CONTROLS THE WITNESS LADDER DEMANDS FOR AN ACCESS WITNESS:

    LIVENESS          three of them.
                      (a) RAM: the same sb/lbu instruction shapes round-trip 0x55
                          through plain RAM, so a device row reading 0x00 could not be
                          blamed on a bad encoding.
                      (b) DEVICE REGISTER: 0x55 -> cyl_lo and 0x66 -> cyl_hi read back
                          as 0x6655 through the wdc's own decode.  This is #481's
                          preserved liveness=0x6655 idiom, kept deliberately so this
                          witness and that one are comparable.
                      (c) per phase: the ARMED status read, which must show DRQ before
                          the poke or the phase measured nothing.

    DEVICE SIGNATURE  two of them.
                      (a) FIFO: push 0x5a then 0xa5 to the data port and read the SAME
                          address twice.  A memory cell returns 0xa5 both times; only a
                          FIFO returns them in push order.
                      (b) STATUS: the byte at +7 is COMPUTED by status_byte() out of
                          diskimage_exist(), d->error and d->write_in_progress.  The
                          guest never wrote it.  RAM would answer with what was stored.

WHY THIS IS ALSO A DETECTOR, NOT ONLY A WITNESS.  Every row carries a want for BOTH
legs.  Phase 2's two rows are the only ones whose want DIFFERS between the legs; every
other row is an identity row that must hold on both.  So the file fails on the committed
build, passes once the handler decodes its offset, and still fails if a future fix
over-reaches: a build that refuses offset 0 as well reds PHASE 1, and a build that keeps
the decode but nulls its effect reds PHASE 2 again.

BYTE ORDER.  evbmips -e malta is LITTLE-endian.  Every access here is a single byte, so
byte order cannot silently change what a row means -- stated because a sibling detector
in this tree was measured testing the wrong endianness.

Usage:  wdcaltoff_rung3_probe.py <base-binary> <fix-binary> <disk-image> [outdir]

BOTH LEGS RUN INSIDE ONE PYTHON INVOCATION, SO THE INSTRUMENT IS IDENTICAL BY
CONSTRUCTION.  A driver shaped "for t in base fix; do python3 probe.py $t; done" gives
the two legs different instruments if the probe is edited between them, and the
difference lands in the very output being diffed.

NOTHING IN THE REPO IS WRITTEN.  Both trees under measurement are copies under /tmp, and
the disk image is attached with the iR: prefix, whose overlay is pid-unique.
"""
import os
import pty
import re
import select
import sys
import time

BASE_BIN = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/tmp/gxaltoff/base/gxemul"
FIX_BIN = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "/tmp/gxaltoff/fix/gxemul"
DISK = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "/tmp/gxaltoff/altoff-scratch.img"
OUTDIR = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else "/tmp/gxaltoff/run"

BASE = 0xffffffff80100000          # KSEG0, physical 0x00100000, inside malta's 128 MB
RAWBIN = None                      # set in main(), lives under OUTDIR

WDC_HI, WDC_LO = 0xb800, 0x01f0    # wdc register file, KSEG1
ALT_HI, ALT_LO = 0xb800, 0x03f6    # wdc_altstatus region, KSEG1
RAM_HI = 0x8020                    # KSEG0 scratch for the RAM liveness control

#  Register offsets from the wdc base -- src/include/thirdparty/wdcreg.h
R_DATA, R_SECCNT, R_SECTOR = 0, 2, 3
R_CYL_LO, R_CYL_HI, R_SDH = 4, 5, 6
R_STATUS = 7                       # wd_command on write, wd_status on read

#  Status bits -- wdcreg.h
DRDY, DSC, DRQ, ERR = 0x40, 0x10, 0x08, 0x01

#  status_byte() ORs DRDY|DSC because diskimage_exist() is true for the attached IDE
#  image; DRQ iff (inbuf_head != inbuf_tail) OR write_in_progress; ERR iff d->error.
#
#  d->error IS SET AT DEVINIT.  Grep it as "->error" -- dev_wdc_init writes
#  "d->error      = 1;" with the field name padded, so a grep for "d->error = 1" with a
#  SINGLE space MATCHES NOTHING and reports that the field starts at 0.  It did, while
#  this file was being written, and the first run's measured 0x51 against a predicted
#  0x50 is what sent me back to look.  A pattern that matches nothing reports zero for
#  everything, which is this project's oldest apparatus trap -- and here the measurement
#  caught the reading rather than the other way round.
#
#  wdc_command() clears it ("d->error = 0" at the top), so the power-on ERR bit stands
#  only until the first phase issues WDCC_WRITE.
ST_POWERON = DRDY | DSC | ERR      # 0x51  before any command has been issued
ST_IDLE = DRDY | DSC               # 0x50  ring empty, no write armed, error cleared
ST_ARMED = DRDY | DSC | DRQ        # 0x58  write_in_progress set

WDCC_WRITE = 0x30                  # wdcreg.h
WDCTL_RST = 0x04
WDCTL_IDS = 0x02
SRST_POKE = WDCTL_IDS | WDCTL_RST  # 0x06 -- what older OpenBSD asserts; #481's value
NIEN_POKE = WDCTL_IDS              # 0x02 -- no reset bit at all

STAGE = [0x71, 0x72, 0x73, 0x74, 0x75, 0x76, 0x77, 0x78]

zero, v0, v1, a0, a1, a2, a3 = 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7
t0, t1, t2, t3 = 8, 9, 10, 11
s0, s1, s2, s3, s4, s5, s6, s7 = 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23
t9 = 25


def I(op, rs, rt, imm):
    return (op << 26) | (rs << 21) | (rt << 16) | (imm & 0xffff)


def lui(rt, imm):
    return I(0x0F, 0, rt, imm)


def ori(rt, rs, imm):
    return I(0x0D, rs, rt, imm)


def addiu(rt, rs, imm):
    return I(0x09, rs, rt, imm)


def sb(rt, off, base):
    return I(0x28, base, rt, off)


def lbu(rt, off, base):
    return I(0x24, base, rt, off)


def beq(rs, rt, off):
    return I(0x04, rs, rt, off)


NOP = 0
NAME = {zero: "zr", v0: "v0", v1: "v1", a0: "a0", a1: "a1", a2: "a2", a3: "a3",
        t0: "t0", t1: "t1", t2: "t2", t3: "t3", s0: "s0", s1: "s1", s2: "s2",
        s3: "s3", s4: "s4", s5: "s5", s6: "s6", s7: "s7", t9: "t9"}

prog = []


def emit(word, mn):
    """mn is checked against the EMULATOR'S OWN disassembly.

    A wrong register field silently yields 0, and 0 is a value several rows below would
    accept by accident -- this project has shipped that mistake into a committed gate.
    """
    prog.append((word, mn))


def e_li(rt, v):
    emit(addiu(rt, zero, v), "addiu %s,zr,%d" % (NAME[rt], v))


def e_sb(rt, off, base):
    emit(sb(rt, off, base), "sb %s,%d(%s)" % (NAME[rt], off, NAME[base]))


def e_lbu(rt, off, base):
    emit(lbu(rt, off, base), "lbu %s,%d(%s)" % (NAME[rt], off, NAME[base]))


def e_store(val, off, base):
    e_li(t3, val)
    e_sb(t3, off, base)


def arm_a_write():
    """Arm WDCC_WRITE and stage STAGE into the input ring.

    wdc_command() -> wdc__write() sets d->write_in_progress = d->cur_command, which is
    what makes status_byte() raise DRQ.  wdc_command() also calls
    wdc_new_command_reset(), so each phase starts from a clean ring on BOTH legs
    regardless of what the previous phase left -- that is what keeps the phases
    independent, and it is why phase 3 measures the same thing on both legs even though
    phase 2 left them in different states.

    len(STAGE) is 8, deliberately NOT a multiple of 512: the sector drain inside
    DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc) fires on "inbuf_len % 512 == 0", so nothing reaches the disk
    image and the staged bytes simply sit in the ring where the reset can destroy them.
    """
    e_store(0xa0, R_SDH, t0)       # drive 0, head 0 (bits 7 and 5 are the obsolete 1s)
    e_store(0x01, R_SECCNT, t0)
    e_store(0x01, R_SECTOR, t0)
    e_store(0x00, R_CYL_LO, t0)
    e_store(0x00, R_CYL_HI, t0)
    e_store(WDCC_WRITE, R_STATUS, t0)
    for b in STAGE:
        e_store(b, R_DATA, t0)


#  ---------------------------------------------------------------- setup
emit(lui(t0, WDC_HI), "lui t0,0xb800")
emit(ori(t0, t0, WDC_LO), "ori t0,t0,0x01f0")
emit(lui(t1, ALT_HI), "lui t1,0xb800")
emit(ori(t1, t1, ALT_LO), "ori t1,t1,0x03f6")
emit(lui(t2, RAM_HI), "lui t2,0x8020")

#  A -- RAM LIVENESS: the same instruction shapes, through plain RAM.
e_store(0x55, 0, t2)
e_lbu(v0, 0, t2)

#  B -- DEVICE-REGISTER LIVENESS: #481's 0x6655, through the wdc's own decode.
e_store(0x55, R_CYL_LO, t0)
e_store(0x66, R_CYL_HI, t0)
e_lbu(v1, R_CYL_LO, t0)
e_lbu(a0, R_CYL_HI, t0)

#  C -- DEVICE SIGNATURE: the data port is a FIFO, not a cell.
e_store(0x5a, R_DATA, t0)
e_store(0xa5, R_DATA, t0)

THE DEFECT IS CONFIRMED AND TWO OF MY\nSUPPORTING PREMISES WERE WRONG.  Corrected here. ***\n\nVerdict: *\"A and B are defects, and both proposed corrections are right.  They are TWO changes under your\nreopening rule.  `apcb_flags is never written' is false; no third destination typo was found.\"*\n\n**CORRECTION 1 -- `apcb_flags' IS WRITTEN, and I filed the opposite as fact.**  This row said it *\"is never\nassigned at all\"*.  `grep -rn apcb_flags src/' returns `cpu_alpha_palcode.c:221' -- **`wrfen' assigns it**\nfrom `r[ALPHA_A0]' and then writes it back to PCB memory, and `swpctx' itself READS the field when saving the\noutgoing context.\n\n**The honest statement is narrower and still a defect:** `swpctx' never assigns `apcb_flags' WHEN LOADING A\nNEW CONTEXT, so the incoming context's flags are silently dropped and the outgoing context's value persists\nacross the switch. I had not\nestablished that, and it is the difference between a reporting bug and a state-corruption bug.\n\n**SCOPE: TWO CHANGES, NOT ONE.**  I intended to fix both in one diff -- same function, same class.  codex\nrules they are two under the reopening rule.  **Accepted**: the observables differ (a guest register versus\ninternal PCB state reachable only through a translation), so one test cannot cover both without a new\nobservation, which is exactly what that rule forbids.\n\n**MY Q3 HYPOTHESIS WAS REFUTED, and recording that matters as much as a finding.**  I said a third\nwrong-destination assignment was *\"more likely than not\"* given two in one function, and asked for the whole\nhandler to be read. Verified by\nreading the lines rather than taken on the seat's word.\n\n`cpu->cd.alpha.ps` has NO explicit initialiser anywhere in `src/`, so it is zero from the zeroed cpu\nstruct and USERMODE is clear -- kernel mode, and the gate does not fire.  **That is a derivation, and\nthe harness turns it into a measurement**: `regress/alpha_harness_probe.py` now carries a `palgate`\nrow asserting the diagnostic is absent, and a `palalive` row asserting the machine survives a swpctx\ncall at all.\n\n*Note the shape: the premise that was wrong is the one I did NOT think to question -- I checked the\ninstruction decoder carefully and never looked inside the function it dispatches to.  That is the\nthird instance this week and it is the subject of the queued rule question\n[[sgilinearnegidxpostmortem]], which asks whether the premise-audit instruction needs a\nself-directed twin.  **This is its third data point and the first where a seat caught it before it\ncost anything.***\n\n**AND THE BRIEF THAT ASKED THIS WAS THE SECOND ATTEMPT.**  The first -- carrying a four-step witness\nDESIGN -- was REFUSED by the same seat as chain-shaped content (see [[codexbriefscoping]]).  The\nchain-free re-ask, which requests a field-by-field audit and names no procedure, was answered in\nfull.  **The design question went to grok instead**, so neither question was dropped.\n\n*** THE WITNESS DESIGN WAS REFUTED, BY THE SEAT THE REFUSED BRIEF WAS ROUTED TO.  grok,\n`regress/artifacts/alphaswpctxptbr/grok_witness_20260907.txt`, 13.5 kB. ***\n\n**VERDICT:** *\"YES, a rung-3 witness is buildable on the three constructing Alpha machines -- but the\nproposed 'no MMU at all, two `swpctx`, read `A+16`' design is unsound as written if `A.flags` is\nnonzero. The one-token fix is not a PAL convention; it is a copy-paste of the previous LHS.\"*\n\n*** THE DESIGN WAS SELF-DEFEATING AND I HAD NOT SEEN IT: THE DEFECT DESTROYS THE PATH THE WITNESS\nNEEDS TO OBSERVE IT. ***  Verified in `memory_alpha.c` rather than taken on the seat's word, and the\nsource is sharper than the verdict:\n\n  * **K0SEG is checked BEFORE `base` is used at all** (`:62`): `if (!userMode && vaddr >=\n    ALPHA_K0SEG_BASE && vaddr <= ALPHA_K0SEG_END) { *return_paddr = vaddr & 0x3ffffffffff; return\n    2; }`.  A K0SEG access never consults `apcb_ptbr`, so grok's remedy is sound.\n    `ALPHA_K0SEG_BASE = 0xfffffc0000000000`; `ALPHA_PHYS_TO_K0SEG(x) = x | BASE`.\n  * **The identity map is an explicit 'UGLY hack' conditioned on `base == 0`** (`:73`).  That is the\n    ONLY reason a naive harness works at all -- `ptbr` is zero at reset.  **The moment the buggy\n    assignment makes `apcb_ptbr` nonzero, `base != 0` and every later access falls into a real\n    page-table walk over garbage**, with an `exit(1)` sitting on one vaddr at `:75-78`.\n  * **AND THE POLARITY TRAP grok did not state, which kills the 'keep flags==0' fallback too:** if\n    the marker is put in `A.ptbr` instead, then under the *FIXED* build `apcb_ptbr` becomes that\n    nonzero marker and the identity map dies on the FIX rather than on the defect.  **Neither\n    polarity survives with a nonzero value anywhere in that field.**  So K0SEG is not the better\n    option, it is the only one.\n\n**THE CORRECTED DESIGN, and it needs no 64-bit immediates:** `lda`/`ldah` build 32-bit constants\nonly, and a K0SEG address needs bit 63..42 set.  The way through is to **load the pointers BEFORE the\nfirst `swpctx`, while the identity map is still alive**: place the 64-bit K0SEG pointers in\nidentity-mapped scratch with the debugger's `put q`, have the guest `ldq` them into registers, and\nonly then issue the calls.  Every access after that carries a K0SEG address in a register and is\nimmune to whatever `apcb_ptbr` becomes.\n\n**A SEPARATE TRAP FOUND WHILE CHECKING THIS, which the harness avoids only by luck:** `memory_alpha.c:87`\nsilently remaps `(vaddr & ~0x1fff) == 0x20000000` to `PROM_ARGSPACE_PADDR` (0x12000).  The harness's\ncode at `0x20010000` and scratch at `0x20020000` fall OUTSIDE that 8 kB window -- but nothing said\nso, and a probe placed 64 kB lower would have had its stores quietly land in PROM argument space.\n\n**Q4 ANSWERED:** *\"The one-token fix is not a PAL convention; it is a copy-paste of the previous\nLHS.\"*  Both seats agree the correction is `apcb_flags` at `cpu_alpha_palcode.c:282`.\n\n*** THE ROUTING WORKED AND IS THE REUSABLE LESSON. ***  codex REFUSED this brief as chain-shaped;\ngrok answered it in full, read the handler, the dispatch path and the existing harness, and refuted\nthe design on a mechanism I had missed.  **The chain-free re-ask to codex and the chain-shaped\noriginal to grok together cost one extra invocation and lost nothing** -- which is the argument the\n2026-09-09 adjudication is asked to rule on under [[codexbriefscoping]].\n\n*** CODE REVIEW OF THE HARNESS, BEFORE ITS FIRST RUN.  grok,\n`regress/artifacts/alphaswpctxptbr/grok_harness_20260907.txt` -- codex REFUSED this brief too (sixth\nrefusal, chain/witness shape), so it is grok's third answer to a brief codex would not take. ***\n\n**VERDICT:** *\"DO NOT TRUST THE FIRST RUN.  The lda/ldah/ldq bootstrap and the swpctx SAVE/RESTORE\nwalk are right.  The encodings that this file actually emits match the decoder.  `put d` is the right\ndebugger command. K0SEG translation is\n`vaddr & 0x3ffffffffff`, so **the K0SEG idea survives contact with `alpha_translate_v2p` and the\nPHYSICAL BACKING does not.**  And the failure mode is silent:\n`memory_warn_about_unimplemented_addr` only halts when `halt_on_nonexistant_memaccess` is set, i.e.\nunder `-T`.  **Without it, writes succeed and are DISCARDED and reads RETURN ZEROS** -- and an\ninstruction fetch of zeros is a real instruction, `call_pal 0`.\n\n**MY ORACLE MADE THAT UNDETECTABLE.**  It asserted `PCB_A+16 == 0` for the correct case, and 0 is\nalso what an unmapped read returns.  **The witness would have gone green having written nothing,\nread nothing, and executed `call_pal 0` off a zero-filled code page.**\n\n**REPAIRED, and the repair is better than moving the addresses:** K0SEG means translation never\nconsults `apcb_ptbr`, so `apcb_ptbr` may now hold a distinctive NONZERO value -- which the FIRST\ndesign could not allow, because a nonzero ptbr killed the identity map.  So:\n\n    correct handler  -> PCB_A+16 == PTBR_VAL  (0xaaaa1111)\n    the defect       -> PCB_A+16 == FLAGS_VAL (0xbbbb2222)\n    anything broken  -> 0, which is NEITHER, so BOTH rows red\n\nplus a third row `swpctx mapped` asserting the value is not 0 -- **because without it a probe whose\naddresses drifted back outside RAM would fail one row and pass the other, which reads exactly like a\nreal defect.**  Addresses moved inside 64 MB with an `assert` that says so.\n\n*** FINDING 2 -- `palalive` IS A CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL, AND I WROTE IT WHILE APPLYING THE RULE\nAGAINST THAT. ***  *\"`alive` is 'the pty is still readable'.  `alpha_palcode`'s default arm does\n`cpu->running = 0` and stays in the debugger because `-V` is single-step. The\npremise was true and understated.\n\n**CONFIRMED, so the design work was not wasted:** encodings match the decoder; the bootstrap method\nis valid and nothing between the `put d` writes and the first `call_pal` touches `apcb_ptbr`; K0SEG\nis checked before `base`; PCB offsets match `struct alpha_pcb`; `ps` is zero from `zeroed_alloc`;\n`0x30` is not on the unprivileged whitelist. Derived 2026-09-07 from the codex fix design on [[lcairqstubkill]] plus this row's\nown witness. ***\n\n**THE TWO LCA ROWS LOOK LIKE ONE PROBLEM AND ARE NOT.**  Both are bare `fatal()+exit(1)` reached by\nordinary guest access, so it is tempting to give them one disposition. Declining is not a lost event; it is the architecturally right reply.\n\n> **So the dispositions properly differ, and the reason is not \"one is worse\".  For a DELIVERY path\n> an unimplemented target has no honest continuation; for an ADDRESSING path it has one, and the\n> tree already implements it.**\n\n*** AND THE TREE ALREADY DOES THE RIGHT THING ONE STEP DOWN, which the witness measured by accident.\n***  The `bus == 0` branch already reaches `bus_pci_setaddr` / `bus_pci_data_access`, and this row's\nown witness recorded the result: **a read of an empty slot returns `0xffffffffffffffff`** (the\n`bus ctlsig` row, MEASURED).  grok noted the same about the armed side in its design review --\n*\"falling through into existing bus_pci with cur_bus=1 (empty type-1 also survives)\"*.\n\n**SO THE LIKELY FIX IS NOT A DECLINE AT ALL BUT A FALL-THROUGH:** stop special-casing `bus != 0`,\nlet the existing `bus_pci` path handle it, and an empty bus 1 answers all-ones by itself. Read that round before designing this one.\n\nsev HIGH on the wiring; it would be CRITICAL if a witness lands, and the row says so rather than\npre-judging it.\n\n*** THE WITNESS-SHAPE QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND FAVOURABLY: THE ASSERT IS GUEST-DRIVEN, NOT\nHOST-TIMER-DRIVEN, SO A STEPPED PROBE CAN REACH IT. ***\n\nThe carrier demands one question before designing any probe around a tick: *what produces the thing\nthe tick consumes?*  If the answer is `timer_add`, the probe must free-run, because `debugger.c`\ncalls `timer_stop()` while interacting and `step N` returns before `timer_start()`.\n\n    DEVICE_TICK(wdc)\n    {\n            struct wdc_data *d = (struct wdc_data *) extra;\n\n            if (d->int_assert)\n                    INTERRUPT_ASSERT(d->irq);\n    }\n\n**What it consumes is `d->int_assert`, a flag the COMMAND PATH sets from an ordinary guest register\nwrite.**  No host timer produces it. the probe steps far\n> enough for the tick to run; `INTERRUPT_ASSERT(d->irq)` dispatches to the registered handler for\n> `<machine>.lca`; and that handler is `fatal()` + `exit(1)`.**  Synchronous in the carrier's sense\n> -- what the tick consumes comes from the guest, not from SIGALRM.\n\n**STILL A PREDICTION, AND THREE LINKS ARE UNVERIFIED:** (1) that `INTERRUPT_ASSERT` on `d->irq`\nresolves to the LCA handler rather than to an intermediate ISA controller that swallows it; Signed left-shift overflow is UNDEFINED BEHAVIOUR in C99 and C11.\n\n*** IT IS NOT AN EDGE CASE -- IT IS THE ONLY PATH THAT WORKS. ***  Two lines below, the model gates on `if (!(tileptr & 0x80000000)) return;' with the comment `The highest bit seems to be set for a \"valid\" tile pointer', and then clears it with `tileptr &= ~0x80000000;'. The UB is on the taken path, not a corner.\n\nGUEST-DRIVABLE: the three arrays are written by ordinary guest register writes inside DEVICE_ACCESS(sgi_re) (the TLB register handlers, which require 8-byte writes), so the guest chooses the value that overflows.\n\nNOT the same defect at the fourth array: `re_linear_a' is `uint32_t[32]', so `re_linear_a[tile_nr] << 12' promotes to UNSIGNED int and wraps rather than overflowing -- defined, and out of scope for this row.\n\nFIX SHAPE: three one-token casts, `(uint32_t)d->re_tlb_x[tile_nr] << 16'. VERDICT: CONFIRMED, AND THE PREVIOUS SEAT'S NUMBERS WERE RIGHT.  OpenBSD 7.6
issues exactly TWELVE byte writes to paddr 0x1400002c and ZERO reads, reproduced
on four independent runs.  Six carry 0x08 (WDCTL_4BIT), five carry 0x02
(WDCTL_IDS), and the FIRST carries 0x0c = WDCTL_RST | WDCTL_4BIT -- so a real ATA
SOFT RESET is among them and is silently discarded today.  The command block at
0x14000000..0x1400000f SUCCEEDS: 12,718 accesses across all eight registers, and
wd0 attaches with correct geometry, so devinit->addr is RIGHT and the defect is a
missing offset case, not a wrong base.  Nothing else in the constructed machine
claims 0x1400002c; the registered wdc_altstatus window at 0x14000206 receives
ZERO accesses for the entire boot.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Q1.  IS IT TWELVE WRITES, AND ARE SIX OF THEM 0x08?      YES to both.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Four runs, two independent instruments, all agreeing:

  A1_pristine_boot.log         12 writes   0 reads     (unmodified build)
  A2_pristine_boot.log         12 writes   0 reads     (unmodified build)
  A3_pristine_boot.log         12 writes   0 reads     (unmodified build)
  B1_hook_full_window.log      12 writes   0 reads     (census-hook build)

All twelve are len=1, all from pc=0x8c15f6e8 <obio_iomem_write_1+0x8>, all with
no_exceptions=0 (real guest stores, not debugger reads).

  *** THE COUNT WAS TAKEN AS OCCURRENCES, NOT LINES, ON PURPOSE.  The emulator's
  warning interleaves with the guest console stream mid-word -- the transcript
  literally reads "wd0 at wdc0 chan[ memory WRITE ... ]nel 0 drive 0".  In these
  four runs both forms happened to give 12, so this is a precaution and NOT a
  measured correction; tally_runs.sh prints both so a divergence would show. ***

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Q2.  WHAT ARE THE ACTUAL VALUES?   0x0c once, then 0x08/0x02 alternating.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
In order (bit names from the tree's own src/include/thirdparty/wdcreg.h --
WDCTL_4BIT 0x08, WDCTL_RST 0x04, WDCTL_IDS 0x02):

   1  0x0c   WDCTL_4BIT | WDCTL_RST      <-- SRST ASSERTED
   2  0x08   WDCTL_4BIT                  <-- SRST released
   3  0x02   WDCTL_IDS
   4  0x08   WDCTL_4BIT
   5  0x02   WDCTL_IDS
   6  0x08   WDCTL_4BIT
   7  0x02   WDCTL_IDS
   8  0x08   WDCTL_4BIT
   9  0x02   WDCTL_IDS
  10  0x08   WDCTL_4BIT
  11  0x02   WDCTL_IDS
  12  0x08   WDCTL_4BIT

  histogram:  0x0c x1   0x08 x6   0x02 x5      carrying WDCTL_RST: 1

Shape: one assert/release soft-reset pair at the head of the channel probe, then
five disable-interrupts / enable-interrupts pairs bracketing PIO commands.
Window context around the 0x0c (from the hook log):

      W  sdh              0xb0     (select drive 1)
      R  status           0x01
      W  sdh              0xa0     (select drive 0)
      W  UNMAPPED +0x2c   0x0c     <<< SRST asserted, DISCARDED
      W  UNMAPPED +0x2c   0x08     <<< SRST released, DISCARDED
      W  sdh              0xa0
      R  status           0x51

CORROBORATED ON THE UNMODIFIED BINARY, with no instrumentation of any kind, by
the tree's own committed write-watchpoint (#250, the debugger watchpoint
command).  It reported paddr 0x1400002c, len 1, value 0x0c first and then the
same {0x08, 0x02} set, from the same pc.  See A4_pristine_watchpoint.log.

  *** THE WATCHPOINT RUN SAW 9 OF THE 12, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE METHOD,
  NOT A DISAGREEMENT.  The check in MEMORY_RW_ONE_PAGE is guarded by
  !single_step && !about_to_enter_single_step, and the hit itself SETS
  about_to_enter_single_step -- so a write arriving before the debugger has been
  entered and resumed is not reported.  It is a LOWER BOUND by construction.  It
  confirms the VALUES; the COUNT of 12 rests on the other two instruments. ***

WHAT MAPPING THE REGISTER WOULD THEN DO (read from DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc_altstatus)):
  * on the 0x0c write, idata & WDCTL_RST is true, so the handler sets
    d->cur_command = COMMAND_RESET and calls wdc_new_command_reset(), which
    clears atapi_cmd_in_progress, atapi_phase and write_in_progress and purges
    the inbuf ring (inbuf_head = inbuf_tail = 0).  The guard is LEVEL-triggered
    by deliberate #481 design.
  * the six 0x08 and five 0x02 writes reach no WDCTL_RST branch; they would
    produce only a debug() line, invisible without -v.
  * reads would return status_byte(), which is PURE (verified by reading it: it
    derives from diskimage_exist, the ring pointers, write_in_progress, d->error
    and the atapi phase, and assigns nothing).  Today they return 0 instead --
    but the guest performs ZERO reads there in this boot, so that half is not
    observable on this rig.
  * cur_command = COMMAND_RESET (0x100) is a LATCH.  Its only two consumers are
    the cyl_lo and cyl_hi read arms, and BOTH are gated on
    diskimage_is_a_cdrom(), so on this IDE-disk rig they do not fire.

  NOT SETTLED: whether delivering the reset changes the boot outcome, and what a
  CD-ROM rig (-d ic:) would do -- both consumers of the latch are cdrom-gated and
  this census used a plain IDE disk.  Those are fix-side measurements the round
  still owes; this census does not answer them.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Q3.  DO THE COMMAND-BLOCK ACCESSES SUCCEED?    YES -- decisively.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THIS IS THE DISCRIMINATING CONTROL AND IT COMES OUT ON THE "MISSING OFFSET CASE"
SIDE.  Full window census from B1_hook_full_window.log (landisk uses addr_mult=2,
so device register N sits at paddr 0x14000000 + 2N):

  paddr        wdc register           dir  len  count
  0x14000000   0 data                 R    2    2560
  0x14000002   1 error/features       R    1       6
  0x14000002   1 error/features       W    1      12
  0x14000004   2 seccnt               R    1       2
  0x14000004   2 seccnt               W    1      13
  0x14000006   3 sector               R    1       2
  0x14000006   3 sector               W    1      12
  0x14000008   4 cyl_lo               R    1       3
  0x14000008   4 cyl_lo               W    1      13
  0x1400000a   5 cyl_hi               R    1       2
  0x1400000a   5 cyl_hi               W    1      13
  0x1400000c   6 sdh                  W    1      33
  0x1400000e   7 status/command       R    1   10033
  0x1400000e   7 status/command       W    1      14
  0x1400002c   *** NOT MAPPED ***     W    1      12
                                              -------
                                               12730   (12718 mapped + 12 not)

Nothing at all in 0x14000010..0x1400002b or 0x1400002d..0x1400003f.

DEVICE-SIGNATURE CONTROL (the value could only have come from the emulated wdc,
not from RAM): the guest reads back the IDENTIFY data and prints

    wd0 at wdc0 channel 0 drive 0: <wdc-scratch-64m.img>
    wd0: 128-sector PIO, CHS, 64MB, 131 cyl, 16 head, 63 sec, 132048 sectors

-- the model string is the host image's filename and the geometry is the one the
emulator computed for it.  RAM cannot produce that.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION: the pristine build run with -v prints the
device's own DATA-register debug line, and it counts 2560 "wdc: read from DATA"
-- byte-for-byte the same number as the hook's 2560 reads at 0x14000000.  Two
instruments, one modified and one not, agreeing exactly.  Also from that run:
0 "wdc: WARNING" of any kind (no flood), and 0 accesses to ALTSTATUS.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Q4.  DOES ANYTHING ELSE CLAIM 0x1400002c?      NO.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Answered on the CONSTRUCTED machine, not just by grep, via the debugger's
device-list command (A5_device_list.log).  Complete map:

   0:            ram @ 0x0c000000  len 0x4000000
   1:            wdc @ 0x14000000  len 0x10        <-- 0x14000000..0x1400000f
   2:  wdc_altstatus @ 0x14000206  len 0x2         <-- 0x14000206..0x14000207
   3:            ram @ 0x1e000000  len 0x8000
   4:         sh4_sq @ 0xe0000000  len 0x4000000
   5..12:  ram / sh4_itlb_aa / sh4_itlb_da1 / sh4_utlb_aa / sh4_utlb_da1
  13:       sh4_pcic @ 0xfe200000  len 0x224
  14:            sh4 @ 0xff000000  len 0x1000000
  15:        rs5c313 @ 0x110000000 len 0x10

0x1400002c falls in no entry.  The command block ends 0x1c bytes below it and
wdc_altstatus begins 0x1da bytes above it.  Static grep agrees: the only source
reference to this range is machine_landisk.c's single device_add of
"wdc ... addr_mult=2 addr=0x14000000", and DEVINIT(wdc) has cases for MACPPC,
HPCMIPS and IQ80321 only.

AND THE REGISTERED WINDOW IS DEAD: the -v run counts ZERO "read from ALTSTATUS"
and ZERO "write to ALT. CTRL" for the whole boot.  So today the handler that
exists is never reached, and the twelve writes that should reach it are discarded
0x1da bytes lower down.

================================================================================
A TRAP WORTH RECORDING -- IT PRODUCED A CLEAN, CONFIDENT, HALF-EMPTY CENSUS
================================================================================
The first version of the census hook tested its window on paddr at do_return_ok.
It reported 12 unmapped writes and ZERO command-block accesses, with no error and
no missing denominator -- and that was wrong.  The device arm of
MEMORY_RW_ONE_PAGE does "paddr -= mem->devices[i].baseaddr" BEFORE calling the
handler, so a device access reaches do_return_ok carrying the RELATIVE offset
(0x00..0x0f), never 0x14000000+.  A window predicate written on paddr is
therefore blind to exactly the mapped half -- which is the half that answers Q3.
The fix is the GXC_P0 latch, taken immediately after address translation.

*** THIS IS PRECISELY HOW A REPORT COULD COME BACK WITH THE UNMAPPED WRITES AND
NO COMMAND-BLOCK CONTROL AT ALL.  A censusing instrument must be shown to see the
POSITIVE case before its negatives are believed; here the 2560/2560 DATA
agreement against the tree's own -v output is that proof. ***

================================================================================
METHOD, AND HOW TO RE-RUN IT
================================================================================
Two builds, neither of them GXEMUL-SEC, neither of them ../build/, and neither
under /tmp/gxwit* (another seat's trees):

  BUILD A  /tmp/gxcensusA   pristine copy of GXEMUL-SEC.  Verified with cmp
                            against SEC file-by-file and [ binary -nt source ]
                            after the build (logs/buildA.log,
                            verify_buildA.sh).  Every number attributed to
                            "pristine" comes from this.
  BUILD B  /tmp/gxcensusB   same tree + a census hook in memory_rw.c ONLY.
                            The complete diff is buildB_census_hook.diff (3
                            hunks); MAKE_RC=0 and FRESH_OK are both recorded in
                            logs/buildB.log.

The emulator is run on the UNMODIFIED -E landisk machine description, no
device_add, no address overrides:

  gxemul -E landisk -M 64 -d iR:_images/wdc-scratch-64m.img \
         _images/openbsd76-landisk-bsd.rd

iR: = IDE, read-only with a pid-unique discard overlay, so runs cannot inherit
state.  Each run boots to the OpenBSD installer prompt ("(I)nstall, (U)pgrade,
(A)utoinstall or (S)hell?") and is then killed; that is the whole probe/attach
phase, and no install is performed.  SCOPE OF EVERY COUNT HERE IS THAT WINDOW.

  run_boot.sh        one boot, output captured (no pty needed; the SCIF console
                     works on a plain pipe)
  census.py          tallies non-existant accesses by paddr, with denominators
  analyse_hook.py    the build-B window census, values and bit decomposition
  tally_runs.sh      cross-run agreement table
  tally_verbose.sh   the -v instrument counts
  watch_2c.py        pristine-build watchpoint capture (pty plumbing is
                     gxprobe.Emu's; install_stubs() is overridden away because
                     that layer is MIPS-specific and this rig is SH4)
  devlist.py         device-list dump on the constructed machine
  verify_buildA.sh   freshness + cmp-against-SEC for build A
  mk_censusB.py      generates the build-B hook (refuses to patch on a
                     non-unique anchor)
  collect.sh         copies every log here

WITNESS LADDER: rung 4 (boot).  A real OpenBSD 7.6 driver reaches the path
unaided on a committed, unmodified machine description, with a liveness control
(the command block answers and the guest completes autoconf) and a device-
signature control (the IDENTIFY data carries the host image's name and geometry,
which RAM cannot produce).

NOT SETTLED, stated rather than guessed:
  * whether delivering the reset changes the boot outcome (a fix-side
    measurement, deliberately not taken here);
  * CD-ROM rig behaviour, where COMMAND_RESET's two cdrom-gated consumers would
    fire;
  * anything past the installer prompt -- no install, no post-attach I/O;
  * other landisk models (machine_landisk.c's own TODO 2) and other guest OS
    versions.  Everything above is OpenBSD 7.6 RAMDISK #70 only.

*** WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DELETED: this row's panel gate was
*** "ship, but not on this packet" PRECISELY BECAUSE the previous warrant rested
*** on an unpreserved artifact.  The re-take preserved everything -- and then the
*** write-up described something the preserved artifact does not show.  That is
*** the same class one step further in: the evidence is there and does not say
*** what the prose says.  Preservation is necessary and not sufficient. ***

OWED, either one: re-take the -v instrument on the disk rig TO COMPLETION and

ALSO CORRECTED: this file reports 0x1400002c as the unmapped site.  It is one of
FIVE per boot, and the other four are real queue items -- 0xfe080000 (5/boot) and
0xfe080040 (1/boot), SH7751R extended-INTC registers reached from intc_init and
intpri_intr_priority; and 0x10000003 (5/boot, rtc_ce) and 0x10000005 (3/boot,
intr_init / extintr_establish), landisk board registers.  census.py PRINTS an
"ALL paddrs" section; this write-up presented only the 0x14000000..0x14000040
window.  Consequence worth stating: fixing 0x1400002c does NOT make `-T` usable
on a landisk boot -- four other sites still halt it -- so any `-T`-based row is a
PROBE row, not a boot row.

issues exactly TWELVE byte writes to paddr 0x1400002c and ZERO reads, reproduced
on four independent runs.  Six carry 0x08 (WDCTL_4BIT), five carry 0x02
(WDCTL_IDS), and the FIRST carries 0x0c = WDCTL_RST | WDCTL_4BIT -- so a real ATA
SOFT RESET is among them and is silently discarded today.  The command block at
0x14000000..0x1400000f SUCCEEDS: 12,718 accesses across all eight registers, and
wd0 attaches with correct geometry, so devinit->addr is RIGHT and the defect is a
missing offset case, not a wrong base.  Nothing else in the constructed machine
claims 0x1400002c; the registered wdc_altstatus window at 0x14000206 receives
ZERO accesses for the entire boot.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Q1.  IS IT TWELVE WRITES, AND ARE SIX OF THEM 0x08?      YES to both.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Four runs, two independent instruments, all agreeing:

  A1_pristine_boot.log         12 writes   0 reads     (unmodified build)
  A2_pristine_boot.log         12 writes   0 reads     (unmodified build)
  A3_pristine_boot.log         12 writes   0 reads     (unmodified build)
  B1_hook_full_window.log      12 writes   0 reads     (census-hook build)

All twelve are len=1, all from pc=0x8c15f6e8 <obio_iomem_write_1+0x8>, all with
no_exceptions=0 (real guest stores, not debugger reads).

  *** THE COUNT WAS TAKEN AS OCCURRENCES, NOT LINES, ON PURPOSE.  The emulator's
  warning interleaves with the guest console stream mid-word -- the transcript
  literally reads "wd0 at wdc0 chan[ memory WRITE ... ]nel 0 drive 0".  In these
  four runs both forms happened to give 12, so this is a precaution and NOT a
  measured correction; tally_runs.sh prints both so a divergence would show. ***

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Q2.  WHAT ARE THE ACTUAL VALUES?   0x0c once, then 0x08/0x02 alternating.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
In order (bit names from the tree's own src/include/thirdparty/wdcreg.h --
WDCTL_4BIT 0x08, WDCTL_RST 0x04, WDCTL_IDS 0x02):

   1  0x0c   WDCTL_4BIT | WDCTL_RST      <-- SRST ASSERTED
   2  0x08   WDCTL_4BIT                  <-- SRST released
   3  0x02   WDCTL_IDS
   4  0x08   WDCTL_4BIT
   5  0x02   WDCTL_IDS
   6  0x08   WDCTL_4BIT
   7  0x02   WDCTL_IDS
   8  0x08   WDCTL_4BIT
   9  0x02   WDCTL_IDS
  10  0x08   WDCTL_4BIT
  11  0x02   WDCTL_IDS
  12  0x08   WDCTL_4BIT

  histogram:  0x0c x1   0x08 x6   0x02 x5      carrying WDCTL_RST: 1

Shape: one assert/release soft-reset pair at the head of the channel probe, then
five disable-interrupts / enable-interrupts pairs bracketing PIO commands.
Window context around the 0x0c (from the hook log):

      W  sdh              0xb0     (select drive 1)
      R  status           0x01
      W  sdh              0xa0     (select drive 0)
      W  UNMAPPED +0x2c   0x0c     <<< SRST asserted, DISCARDED
      W  UNMAPPED +0x2c   0x08     <<< SRST released, DISCARDED
      W  sdh              0xa0
      R  status           0x51

CORROBORATED ON THE UNMODIFIED BINARY, with no instrumentation of any kind, by
the tree's own committed write-watchpoint (#250, the debugger watchpoint
command).  It reported paddr 0x1400002c, len 1, value 0x0c first and then the
same {0x08, 0x02} set, from the same pc.  See A4_pristine_watchpoint.log.

  *** THE WATCHPOINT RUN SAW 9 OF THE 12, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE METHOD,
  NOT A DISAGREEMENT.  The check in MEMORY_RW_ONE_PAGE is guarded by
  !single_step && !about_to_enter_single_step, and the hit itself SETS
  about_to_enter_single_step -- so a write arriving before the debugger has been
  entered and resumed is not reported.  It is a LOWER BOUND by construction.  It
  confirms the VALUES; the COUNT of 12 rests on the other two instruments. ***

WHAT MAPPING THE REGISTER WOULD THEN DO (read from DEVICE_ACCESS(wdc_altstatus)):
  * on the 0x0c write, idata & WDCTL_RST is true, so the handler sets
    d->cur_command = COMMAND_RESET and calls wdc_new_command_reset(), which
    clears atapi_cmd_in_progress, atapi_phase and write_in_progress and purges
    the inbuf ring (inbuf_head = inbuf_tail = 0).  The guard is LEVEL-triggered
    by deliberate #481 design.
  * the six 0x08 and five 0x02 writes reach no WDCTL_RST branch; they would
    produce only a debug() line, invisible without -v.
  * reads would return status_byte(), which is PURE (verified by reading it: it
    derives from diskimage_exist, the ring pointers, write_in_progress, d->error
    and the atapi phase, and assigns nothing).  Today they return 0 instead --
    but the guest performs ZERO reads there in this boot, so that half is not
    observable on this rig.
  * cur_command = COMMAND_RESET (0x100) is a LATCH.  Its only two consumers are
    the cyl_lo and cyl_hi read arms, and BOTH are gated on
    diskimage_is_a_cdrom(), so on this IDE-disk rig they do not fire.

  NOT SETTLED: whether delivering the reset changes the boot outcome, and what a
  CD-ROM rig (-d ic:) would do -- both consumers of the latch are cdrom-gated and
  this census used a plain IDE disk.  Those are fix-side measurements the round
  still owes; this census does not answer them.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Q3.  DO THE COMMAND-BLOCK ACCESSES SUCCEED?    YES -- decisively.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
THIS IS THE DISCRIMINATING CONTROL AND IT COMES OUT ON THE "MISSING OFFSET CASE"
SIDE.  Full window census from B1_hook_full_window.log (landisk uses addr_mult=2,
so device register N sits at paddr 0x14000000 + 2N):

  paddr        wdc register           dir  len  count
  0x14000000   0 data                 R    2    2560
  0x14000002   1 error/features       R    1       6
  0x14000002   1 error/features       W    1      12
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""watch_2c.py -- capture the VALUES written to landisk paddr 0x1400002c on the
PRISTINE (unmodified) build, using the tree's own committed write-watchpoint
(#250, memory_rw.c / debugger_cmds.c).  No source modification of any kind.

WHY A WATCHPOINT AND NOT A GREP: the "non-existant paddr=..." warning prints
direction, length and pc but NOT the value.  The watchpoint fatal() prints the
value bytes.  It is checked BEFORE the device/RAM dispatch, so it sees mapped
and unmapped addresses alike.

The watchpoint enters the debugger after the offending instruction, so this
driver must `continue` once per hit.  Address is given as 0xb400002c -- the P2
(uncached) alias -- so the debugger's v2p succeeds and yields paddr 0x1400002c
without the "couldn't translate" fallback.

PTY PLUMBING IS gxprobe.Emu's, per the standing rule.  install_stubs() is
overridden away because it installs MIPS instruction stubs into a MIPS scratch
address; this rig is SH4 and needs none of that layer.
"""
import os, re, sys, time

sys.path.insert(0, "/mnt/c/DocumentNoSnc/CC/GXEMUL/_scratchpad")
import gxprobe

BIN = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/tmp/gxcensusA/gxemul"
OUT = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "/tmp/census_A_watch.log"
WATCH = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "0xb400002c"
IMG = "/mnt/c/DocumentNoSnc/CC/GXEMUL/_images"


class SH4Emu(gxprobe.Emu):
    def install_stubs(self):
        pass                      # MIPS-only layer; this rig is SH4


argv = ["-V", "-E", "landisk", "-M", "64",
        "-d", "iR:%s/wdc-scratch-64m.img" % IMG,
        "%s/openbsd76-landisk-bsd.rd" % IMG]

e = SH4Emu(BIN, argv, boot_wait=6.0)
e.send("watchpoint add %s, 1" % WATCH, wait=1.0)
e.send("watchpoint show", wait=1.0)

#  Drive to the installer prompt, `continue`ing past each watchpoint stop.
#  The loop is bounded in BOTH directions: at most MAXC continues and at most
#  DEADLINE seconds, so a rig that stops hitting the watchpoint still ends.
MAXC, DEADLINE = 60, 300.0
t0 = time.time()
seen = 0
for i in range(MAXC):
    if time.time() - t0 > DEADLINE:
        print("DEADLINE reached after %d continues" % i)
        break
    e.send("continue", wait=6.0)
    txt = e.raw_text
    n = txt.count("WATCHPOINT:")
    if "(I)nstall" in txt:
        print("installer prompt reached after %d continues (%d hits)" % (i + 1, n))
        break
    if n == seen:
        #  no new hit in this window -- give it one longer drain before giving up
        e.drain(10.0)
        txt = e.raw_text
        if txt.count("WATCHPOINT:") == seen and "(I)nstall" not in txt:
            print("no new hit after continue %d; stopping" % (i + 1))
            break
    seen = txt.count("WATCHPOINT:")

txt = e.raw_text
open(OUT, "w").write(txt)
e.close()

pat = re.compile(r"WATCHPOINT: write of (\d+) byte\(s\) to vaddr 0x([0-9a-f]+) "
                 r"\(paddr 0x([0-9a-f]+)\) = ([0-9a-f ]+?), pc = 0x([0-9a-f]+)")
hits = pat.findall(txt)
print()
print("DENOMINATORS: transcript bytes=%d, 'WATCHPOINT:' occurrences=%d, regex hits=%d"
      % (len(txt), txt.count("WATCHPOINT:"), len(hits)))
print()
print("#   len  vaddr       paddr       value  pc")
import collections
vals = collections.Counter()
for i, (ln, va, pa, val, pc) in enumerate(hits, 1):
    print("%-3d %-4s 0x%-9s 0x%-9s 0x%-4s 0x%s" % (i, ln, va, pa, val.strip(), pc))
    vals[val.strip()] += 1
print()
print("VALUE HISTOGRAM at %s:" % WATCH)
for v in sorted(vals):
    print("   0x%s  x%d" % (v, vals[v]))
print("WATCH_TOTAL=%d" % len(hits))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""#441 DETECTOR: SH4_BCR2 / SH4_BCR3 service a non-16-bit guest access instead
of terminating the emulator.

Rung 3.  Real SH-4 guest instructions through real address decode, real
`memory_rw` and real device dispatch, on an UNMODIFIED in-tree `-E landisk`.
No source is edited, no `device_add` of our own, no boot.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT.  The pre-fix WITNESS (`_scratchpad/_opusseat_sh4_bcr2_
probe.py`) asserted the SYMPTOM -- "a 4-byte store kills the host" -- and so it
goes red once the defect is gone, which is what a witness should do.  This file
is the DETECTOR: it asserts the FIXED behaviour, fails on the pre-fix build, and
is built specifically to fail on the mutants a pass-1 seat produced against the
fix.  Grading one by the other's clauses is a category error in either direction.

    D0  every arm produced data              (absent data must FAIL, not pass)
    D1  4-byte write reaches the register, masked
    D2  4-byte read returns it in its own lane
    D3  a 1-byte write is NOT promoted to 16 bits
    D4  BOTH sites carry the LATCHED form, in ONE process
    D5  a second non-16-bit access in one process survives
    D6  a 4-byte READ is diagnosed too, not only a write
    D8  BCR3's write path still reaches its register

(D7, the big-endian lane, needs a `byte_order(big)` config file and is left to
the round record rather than run here -- see the note at the foot of this file.)

*** D4's ORACLE IS NOT THE REGISTER NAME, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. ***  A
two-character mutant sharing one latch flag between the sites (`[site]` ->
`[0]`) passed a 13-row detector whose D4 asked "does the string BCR3 appear?",
because the DEMOTED `debug()` prints the same name.  Worse, under the cold
debugger `single_step` is true, so `debug()`'s `quiet_mode` early-out never
fires and a probe run this way CANNOT distinguish `fatal()` from `debug()` by
presence at all.  D4 counts the latched suffix instead.

usage: sh4_bsc_width_probe.py <gxemul-binary> <landisk-kernel>
"""
import os
import pty
import re
import select
import sys
import time

BIN = sys.argv[1]
KERNEL = sys.argv[2]

CODE = 0x8c010000
DEST = 0x8c010100
BCR1 = 0xff800000
BCR2 = 0xff800004
#  #441: BCR3 is 0xff800050, NOT 0xff800006.  The pass-1 brief asserted the
#  latter without opening sh4_bscreg.h:70, and the three packet-fed seats -- which
#  by construction cannot check a fact the packet gets wrong -- built whole
#  designs on the imagined adjacency, while every seat that could open the header
#  caught it.  The two registers do not share an access window.
BCR3 = 0xff800050

MOV_L_R0_AT_R1 = 0x2102   # mov.l r0,@r1
MOV_L_R0_AT_R2 = 0x2202   # mov.l r0,@r2
MOV_W_R0_AT_R1 = 0x2101   # mov.w r0,@r1
MOV_B_R0_AT_R1 = 0x2100   # mov.b r0,@r1
MOV_B_AT_R1_R4 = 0x6410   # mov.b @r1,r4  (sign-extends)
MOV_L_AT_R1_R2 = 0x6212   # mov.l @r1,r2
MOV_W_AT_R1_R2 = 0x6211   # mov.w @r1,r2   (sign-extends)
MOV_L_R2_AT_R3 = 0x2322   # mov.l r2,@r3
LATCHED = "(reported once per register)"


#  #441 pass 2: the big-endian arm needs a CONFIG FILE, because byte_order() has no -E
#  equivalent.  emul.c applies the override AFTER the ELF's own byte order, so the
#  `cpu: SH7751R (Little-endian)` banner it prints is stale and must not be used as the
#  control -- BE0 below stores a known word and reads the BYTES back instead.
BE_CONF = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                       ".sh4_bsc_be.conf.tmp")


def write_be_conf():
    with open(BE_CONF, "w") as f:
        f.write('machine(\n\tname("be-landisk")\n\ttype("landisk")\n'
                '\tbyte_order("big")\n\tmemory(64)\n\tload("%s")\n)\n'
                % os.path.abspath(KERNEL))
    return BE_CONF


def session(cmds, nstep, be=False):
    """One cold-debugger session.  Returns (buf, alive)."""
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        if be:
            os.execvp(BIN, [BIN, "-V", "@" + write_be_conf()])
        else:
            os.execvp(BIN, [BIN, "-V", "-E", "landisk", "-M", "64", KERNEL])
        os._exit(127)
    buf = ""
    died = [False]

    def rd(t=0.4):
        nonlocal buf
        r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], t)
        if fd not in r:
            return True
        try:
            d = os.read(fd, 65536)
        except OSError:
            died[0] = True
            return False
        if not d:
            died[0] = True
            return False
        buf += d.decode("latin1", "replace")
        return True

    def wait(mark=0, echo=None, timeout=60):
        t = time.time()

/*
 *  memory_warn_about_unimplemented_addr():
 *
 *  Called from memory_rw whenever memory outside of the physical address space
 *  is accessed.
 */
bool memory_warn_about_unimplemented_addr(struct cpu *cpu, struct memory *mem,
	int writeflag, uint64_t paddr, size_t len)
{
	/*
	 *  HACK: This allows guest OS kernels to probe memory a few KBs past
	 *  the end of memory, without giving too many warnings.
	 */
	if (paddr < mem->physical_max + 0x40000)
		return false;

	int verbosity = VERBOSITY_WARNING;
	if (cpu->machine->halt_on_nonexistant_memaccess)
		verbosity = VERBOSITY_ERROR;

	// ERROR is always "enough", so we will print in that case.
	if (!ENOUGH_VERBOSITY(SUBSYS_MEMORY, verbosity))
		return false;

	uint64_t offset;
	char* symbol = get_symbol_name(&cpu->machine->symbol_context, cpu->pc, &offset);

	// Not the prettiest, but should work fine.
	if (cpu->is_32bit)
		debugmsg_cpu(cpu, SUBSYS_MEMORY,
		    writeflag ? "WRITE" : "READ",
		    verbosity, "%s non-existant "
			"paddr=0x%08" PRIx32 " len=%i pc=0x%08" PRIx32 "%s%s%s",
		    writeflag ? "to" : "from",
		    (uint32_t) paddr,
		    len,
		    (uint32_t) cpu->pc,
		    symbol ? " <" : "",
		    symbol ? symbol : "",
		    symbol ? ">" : "");
	else
		debugmsg_cpu(cpu, SUBSYS_MEMORY,
		    writeflag ? "WRITE" : "READ",
		    verbosity, "%s non-existant "
			"paddr=0x%016" PRIx64 " len=%i pc=0x%016" PRIx64 "%s%s%s",
		    writeflag ? "to" : "from",
		    (uint64_t) paddr,
		    len,
		    (uint64_t) cpu->pc,
		    symbol ? " <" : "",
		    symbol ? symbol : "",
		    symbol ? ">" : "");

	if (cpu->machine->halt_on_nonexistant_memaccess) {
		// Halt all CPUs, even though the bad memory access was on
		// just one of them.
		for (int i = 0; i < cpu->machine->ncpus; ++i)
			cpu->machine->cpus[i]->running = 0;

		return true;
	}

	return false;
}


/*
 *  dump_mem_string():
 *
 *  Dump the contents of emulated RAM as readable text.  Bytes that aren't
 *  readable are dumped in [xx] notation, where xx is in hexadecimal.
 *  Dumping ends after DUMP_MEM_STRING_MAX bytes, or when a terminating
 *  zero byte is found.
 */
#define DUMP_MEM_STRING_MAX	45
void dump_mem_string(struct cpu *cpu, uint64_t addr)
{
	int i;
	for (i=0; i<DUMP_MEM_STRING_MAX; i++) {
		unsigned char ch = '\0';

		cpu->memory_rw(cpu, cpu->mem, addr + i, &ch, sizeof(ch),
		    MEM_READ, CACHE_DATA | NO_EXCEPTIONS);
		if (ch == '\0')
			return;
		if (ch >= ' ' && ch < 126)
			debug("%c", ch);  
		else
			debug("[%02x]", ch);
	}
}


/*
 *  store_byte():
 *
 *  Stores a byte in emulated ram. (Helper function.)
 */
void store_byte(struct cpu *cpu, uint64_t addr, uint8_t data)
{
	if ((addr >> 32) == 0)
		addr = (int64_t)(int32_t)addr;
	cpu->memory_rw(cpu, cpu->mem,
	    addr, &data, sizeof(data), MEM_WRITE, CACHE_DATA);
}


/*
 *  store_string():
 *
 *  Stores chars into emulated RAM until a zero byte (string terminating
 *  character) is found. The zero byte is also copied.
 *  (strcpy()-like helper function, host-RAM-to-emulated-RAM.)
 */
void store_string(struct cpu *cpu, uint64_t addr, const char *s)
{
	do {
		store_byte(cpu, addr++, *s);
	} while (*s++);
}


/*
 *  add_environment_string():
 *
 *  Like store_string(), but advances the pointer afterwards. The most
 *  obvious use is to place a number of strings (such as environment variable
 *  strings) after one-another in emulated memory.
 */
void add_environment_string(struct cpu *cpu, const char *s, uint64_t *addr)
{
	store_string(cpu, *addr, s);
	(*addr) += strlen(s) + 1;
}


/*
 *  add_environment_string_dual():
 *
 *  Add "dual" environment strings, one for the variable name and one for the
 *  value, and update pointers afterwards.
 */
void add_environment_string_dual(struct cpu *cpu,
	uint64_t *ptrp, uint64_t *addrp, const char *s1, const char *s2)
{
	uint64_t ptr = *ptrp, addr = *addrp;

	store_32bit_word(cpu, ptr, addr);
	ptr += sizeof(uint32_t);
	if (addr != 0) {
		store_string(cpu, addr, s1);
		addr += strlen(s1) + 1;
	}
	store_32bit_word(cpu, ptr, addr);
	ptr += sizeof(uint32_t);
	if (addr != 0) {
		store_string(cpu, addr, s2);
		addr += strlen(s2) + 1;
	}

	*ptrp = ptr;
	*addrp = addr;
}

/*
 *  translate_via_mmu():
 *
 *  Scan the UTLB for a matching virtual address. If a match was found, then
 *  check permission bits etc. If everything was ok, then return the physical
 *  page address, otherwise cause an exception.
 *
 *  The implementation should (hopefully) be quite complete, except for lack
 *  of "Multiple matching entries" detection. (On a real CPU, these would
 *  cause exceptions.)
 *
 *  Same return values as sh_translate_v2p().
 */
static int translate_via_mmu(struct cpu *cpu, uint32_t vaddr,
	uint64_t *return_paddr, int flags)
{
	int wf = flags & FLAG_WRITEFLAG;
	int i, urb, urc, require_asid_match, cur_asid, expevt = 0;
	uint32_t hi, lo = 0, mask = 0;
	int sh;		/*  Shared  */
	int d;		/*  Dirty bit  */
	int v;		/*  Valid bit  */
	int pr;		/*  Protection  */
	int i_start;

	cur_asid = cpu->cd.sh.pteh & SH4_PTEH_ASID_MASK;
	require_asid_match = !(cpu->cd.sh.mmucr & SH4_MMUCR_SV)
	    || !(cpu->cd.sh.sr & SH_SR_MD);

	if (!(flags & FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS)) {
		/*
		 *  Increase URC every time the UTLB is accessed.
		 *
		 *  THE TODO THAT USED TO SIT HERE IS ANSWERED, 2026-08-22,
		 *  against a real SH7750 Hardware Manual (Rev.7.00,
		 *  REJ09B0366-0700) obtained by owner directive.  It asked
		 *  whether URC should be left alone by `ldtlb`, wondered
		 *  whether this was the right place, and floated setting it
		 *  to a random value instead.  The MMUCR field definition
		 *  settles all three:
		 *
		 *      "URC is incremented each time the UTLB is accessed.
		 *       When URB > 0, URC is reset to 0 when the condition
		 *       URC = URB occurs. ...  URC is not incremented by an
		 *       LDTLB instruction."
		 *
		 *  So the suspicion was RIGHT and the random-value idea was
		 *  WRONG -- and this code already conforms, by construction
		 *  rather than by intent: X(ldtlb) in cpu_sh_instr.c reads
		 *  URC out of MMUCR and indexes utlb_hi[]/utlb_lo[] itself,
		 *  never entering this translation path, so no increment can
		 *  happen there.  Nothing to change; the TODO simply never
		 *  knew.  The wrap below also matches the quoted text.
		 */
		urb = (cpu->cd.sh.mmucr & SH4_MMUCR_URB_MASK) >>
		    SH4_MMUCR_URB_SHIFT;
		urc = (cpu->cd.sh.mmucr & SH4_MMUCR_URC_MASK) >>
		    SH4_MMUCR_URC_SHIFT;

		/*  fatal("urc = %i  ==>  ", urc);  */
		urc ++;
		if (urc >= SH_N_UTLB_ENTRIES || (urb > 0 && urc == urb))
			urc = 0;
		/*  fatal("%i\n", urc);  */

		cpu->cd.sh.mmucr &= ~SH4_MMUCR_URC_MASK;
		cpu->cd.sh.mmucr |= (urc << SH4_MMUCR_URC_SHIFT);
	}

	/*
	 *  When doing Instruction lookups, the ITLB should be scanned first.
	 *  This is done by using negative i. (Ugly hack, but works.)
	 */
	if (flags & FLAG_INSTR)
		i_start = -SH_N_ITLB_ENTRIES;
	else
		i_start = 0;

	for (i=i_start; i<SH_N_UTLB_ENTRIES; i++) {
		if (i<0) {
			hi = cpu->cd.sh.itlb_hi[i + SH_N_ITLB_ENTRIES];
			lo = cpu->cd.sh.itlb_lo[i + SH_N_ITLB_ENTRIES];
		} else {
			hi = cpu->cd.sh.utlb_hi[i];
			lo = cpu->cd.sh.utlb_lo[i];
		}
		mask = 0xfff00000;

		v = lo & SH4_PTEL_V;
		if (!v)
			continue;

		switch (lo & SH4_PTEL_SZ_MASK) {
		case SH4_PTEL_SZ_1K:  mask = 0xfffffc00; break;
		case SH4_PTEL_SZ_4K:  mask = 0xfffff000; break;
		case SH4_PTEL_SZ_64K: mask = 0xffff0000; break;
		/*  case SH4_PTEL_SZ_1M:  mask = 0xfff00000; break;  */
		}

		if ((hi & mask) != (vaddr & mask))
			continue;

		sh = lo & SH4_PTEL_SH;

		if (!sh && require_asid_match) {
			int asid = hi & SH4_PTEH_ASID_MASK;
			if (asid != cur_asid)
				continue;
		}

		/*  Note/TODO: Check for multiple matches is not implemented. */

		break;
	}

	/*  Virtual address not found? Then it's a TLB miss.  */
	if (i == SH_N_UTLB_ENTRIES)
		goto tlb_miss;

	/*  Matching address found! Let's see whether it is
	    readable/writable, etc.:  */
	d = lo & SH4_PTEL_D? 1 : 0;
	pr = (lo & SH4_PTEL_PR_MASK) >> SH4_PTEL_PR_SHIFT;

	*return_paddr = (vaddr & ~mask) | (lo & mask & 0x1fffffff);

	if (flags & FLAG_INSTR) {
		/*
		 *  Instruction access:
		 */

Name        Source

def dumped(buf):
    m = re.findall(r"0x0*[0-9a-f]+\s+([0-9a-f]{8})", buf or "")
    return m[-1] if m else None


def poke(addr, halfwords):
    """Plant instruction halfwords at CODE and point pc at them."""
    return ["put h 0x%x, 0x%04x" % (CODE + 2 * i, hw)
            for i, hw in enumerate(halfwords)] + ["pc=0x%x" % CODE]

#  Write 0x89ab3ffd as ONE 4-byte store, then read it back 16-bit.  On a
#  little-endian guest the register's own two bytes are idata[15:0], so the
#  device must hold 0x3ffd & 0x3ffd.  Pre-fix this arm KILLS THE HOST.
#  *** THE VALUE IS 0xc003 AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS ROW. ***  It was 0x3ffd,
#  and 0x3ffd & 0x3ffd == 0x3ffd -- so a row NAMED "masked" could not see the mask, and
#  deleting `& 0x3ffd` passed 9/9.  0xc003 & 0x3ffd == 0x0001, so the masked and unmasked
#  results differ in every byte.  Pick oracle VALUES that the transform actually moves.
